meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen's zero, Hale. Who decided it, and was he heard first?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.

Pretty conclusive. The company that makes that checker says in writing it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student, and I have their guide in my bag. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now show me what you have besides that machine's number.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing those down. Owen wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in, which is how half his generation works.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
Turn it this way. A seventeen-year-old who misremembers a line is careless, not dishonest.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds in two weeks. Whatever happens from here, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Five minutes after class and your own notes about it are your impressions, not his work. Being stuck is a fair way for a tired seventeen-year-old to put it. Print me the September piece, with the mark on it.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Then it's 4.4, in writing tonight, with the September piece attached. He'll sit it to put this behind him, not because he did anything, and it gets marked before December 1.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday after school. Who else will be in that room?
Do we have an agreement?
When you tell me who's supervising, yes: Thursday, private, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, and all of it in my inbox tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will complete a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes under procedure 4.4 this Thursday, November 12, after school, that its mark replaces the zero and will be entered before December 1, and that nothing goes on his record. I still require that agreement in writing with his September in-class piece attached, and the name of whoever will supervise him on Thursday. I expect all of this in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants it all in writing tonight with the September sample attached and the supervisor named; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its exact times and how the text arrived, because it was dated, came from Owen's own document, and was something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Opening with the checker score and calling it conclusive, because it handed her the one argument she had come prepared to win and put her on the attack.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the essay being created and filled in between 11:31 PM and midnight on October 28, a late October night very close to what she saw; that proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked who else would be in the room on Thursday, name the supervisor right away so her agreement closes without a condition still hanging over it.
